title: Variable credit buckets + timed upgrade CTAs to increase PLG conversion for free tier
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description: Run an A/B experiment that assigns new signups to staggered credit buckets (Conservative=1k tokens, Standard=5k tokens, Generous=20k tokens) plus a time-limited 'Use-by' CTA surface in the Console and a sequence of 2 emails. Goal is to test whether variable initial credit size combined with urgency-driven CTA placements increases paid conversion within 30 days while controlling for cost and support load. This ticket owners the experiment design, instrumentation, rollout orchestration, and coordination with Design/Engineering/Data. The experiment must include guardrails for enterprise trial requests and surface a handles for legal/contract intake if a high-touch lead is detected.
experiment_design: Randomized assignment at signup (1:1:1 split). Primary metric: proportion of accounts that convert to paid within 30 days of signup. Secondary metrics: 7-day MAU, average tokens consumed, support ticket rate per 1k accounts, cost-per-conversion. Use sequential analysis with a fixed horizon of 30 days and pre-registered stopping rules. Minimum detectable effect targeted: 1.2x baseline conversion (baseline ~2.5%). Estimated per-arm sample size: 25k signups for 80% power. Stratify by signup source (organic, paid, marketplace).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Instrumentation emits events for credit_allocation, credit_usage, cta_impression, cta_click, upgrade_started, upgrade_completed. 2) Dashboard shows primary and secondary metrics per arm with segments by signup source. 3) No regression in enterprise signup funnel or security questionnaire flow. 4) Experiment runs for minimum of 30 days or until pre-registered stopping rule triggers. 5) Product/Design/Eng sign-off on rollout decision and next steps.
implementation_notes: Backend: feature flag + allocation service to assign credit bucket and expiration timestamp at account create.
Billing: ensure upgrade flow consumes remaining credits correctly and that refunds/credit carryover logic is clear.
Console UX: add top banner CTA with countdown, in-product modal with one-click upgrade and price preview.
Email: two-step drip — day 5 'You've got X credits left' and day 14 'Use-by: upgrade for uninterrupted access' with tracking tokens.
Instrumentation: emit standardized events (credit_allocated, credit_spent, cta_shown, cta_clicked, upgrade_initiated, upgrade_completed) to analytics pipeline.
Data: prebuild dashboard queries and anomaly monitors; prepare SQL snippets for cohort joins and SSO-exempt enterprise flags.
Design: create variants of countdown messaging and visual emphasis — A: hard countdown, B: soft recommendation.
Safety: add soft caps to prevent abuse (rate-limit huge credit consumption) and monitor for fraudulent signup spikes.
Legal: flag accounts that hit enterprise thresholds (>50k tokens/day) for contract intake and security questionnaire outreach.
Release plan: feature-flag rollout, dark launch for 48h internal test, open to 100% of new signups via allocation when ready.
Rollback: turn off allocation service and expire banners; revert billing hooks if upgrade flow issues detected.
Owner contacts: PM Aisha Banerjee, Eng lead Marco Ruiz, Design lead Lena Hoffman, Data lead Priya Shah.
risks_and_mitigation: Cost risk: generous bucket may increase free consumption — mitigate via per-account soft caps and monitor cost-per-conversion closely.
Enterprise leakage: some high-value leads might convert via self-serve incorrectly — ensure contract intake flagged and sales notified when thresholds hit.
Instrumentation gaps: missing events will invalidate analysis — add smoke tests and data validation runs before launch.
Support load: increased confusion about credit expiry — prepare updated FAQ, in-product help, and support playbook.
UX regression: CTA could annoy existing power users — keep experiment limited to new signups only and run a negative-feedback monitor.
Regulatory/security: ensure credit emails and banners do not expose contractual terms; confirm with legal and security that messaging is compliant.
Statistical: early peeking can produce false positives — enforce pre-registered stopping rules and consult Data science before decisioning.

notes: This experiment is intentionally scoped to new signups (not existing accounts) and is designed to surface urgency-driven upgrade prompts while learning the elasticity of conversion to credit size. If conversion lifts materially with acceptable unit economics, follow-up work will be a pricing experiment alongside enterprise packaging to offer mid-tier reserved capacity.
